_about: THE BOSS NEEDS TO GO. Two capos plot to take the chair. You hear whispers; you can find out, sit them down, or ignore it. Uncover it and stop it, then whack them or try. With proper planning they die; rush it and one may get away. Ignore it and they make their move. Written from the owner's idea, 2026-10-28.

scenes.title: The old man's tired
scenes.text: {ear.call} waits until the bartender goes in the back. "Boss, I don't like saying it. {lead.call} and {second.call} had a table at the Shamrock last night, the back room, with two fellas from Philly I never seen. I heard {lead.first} say it plain: the old man's tired. Then they saw me and changed the subject to the Phillies."

choices.label: Put a guy on both of them, quiet
choices.hint: Two weeks of watching. If they smell it, they move faster.
choices.result: Your man stayed on them. He came back white as a sheet.
choices.failText: {lead.first} made the tail on Pacific and waved at him. They know you know.

choices.label: Call them both in. Look them in the eye
choices.hint: Sometimes a man only needs to know you heard.

opinion.why: The boss gave us a chance to come clean

choices.result: {lead.first} kissed your cheek and swore on his mother. {second.first} couldn't look at you. For now it's over.
choices.failText: They both swore on their mothers. Neither of them meant it, and now they know their time is short.

choices.label: Old men talk. Let it go

opinion.why: I stuck my neck out and he shrugged

scenes.title: After the Feast
scenes.text: It's worse than talk. {lead.call} has two shooters from Philadelphia on his payroll and a date: the Sunday after the Feast, when you walk out of St. Ann's. {second.call} brings the car. Philly gets your rackets on Pacific and {lead.first} gets your chair. Your man has the license plate written on a matchbook.

choices.label: Do it right: two weeks, the right men, the same night for both
choices.hint: Proper planning. They won't see it coming.
choices.result: You give the job to men who have never missed. Nobody says a word for two weeks.

choices.label: Move tonight, before they do
choices.hint: Fast is dangerous. One of them may slip away.

plus.why: he sleeps in a different bed every night

whack.why: Found in the trunk of his own car on the causeway.
Never came home from the Shamrock.

crew.why: The boss took care of it himself

whack.why: Never came home from the Shamrock.

choices.result: By morning both of them were gone. Nobody on Pacific Avenue says their names anymore.
choices.failText: {second.first} is gone. {lead.first} was out the bathroom window of the Shamrock in his socks. He's on the road to Philadelphia.

choices.label: Take it to Philadelphia first
choices.hint: If they bless it, nobody comes for you after. If they're in on it…

whack.why: Philadelphia gave its blessing. He went for a ride and didn't come back.

choices.result: Philadelphia said: it's your house, clean it. {lead.first} went for a ride. {second.first} begged, and you let him leave town.
choices.failText: Philadelphia said they'd think about it. By the next morning {lead.first} knew you'd been to see them.

choices.label: Sit on it and watch your back
choices.hint: You'll be walking out of church in a few weeks.

scenes.title: The night it ends
scenes.text: Two weeks of watching. You know where {lead.call} eats on Thursdays and where {second.call} parks. The men are in place. The car is clean. All anybody needs is your nod.

choices.label: Give the nod

plus.why: you've had eyes on them for a month

whack.why: Shot at his usual table at the Thursday clam bar. Nobody saw anything.
Never got out of his car.
Never got out of his car.

choices.result: Thursday night, two places, eleven minutes apart. In the morning the Daily Tide called it a robbery.
choices.failText: {second.first} is done. {lead.first} didn't come to the clam bar. Somebody tipped him.

choices.label: Call it off. Make peace instead
choices.hint: They'll know how close they came.

scenes.title: He got away
scenes.text: Word from Philadelphia: {lead.call} is living over a bakery on Passyunk Avenue, telling anybody who'll listen what he knows about your books. Every week he breathes is a week the feds might find him first.

choices.label: Send two men to Passyunk Avenue

plus.why: he never sits with his back to the door

whack.why: Found in the alley behind a bakery in South Philadelphia.

choices.result: It's finished. The bakery opened at six like always.
choices.failText: He saw them coming and went to the FBI's door instead. Now he has company.

choices.label: Put a price on him and let the street do it
Let him rot in Philadelphia
choices.hint: He's not your problem as long as he keeps his mouth shut.

scenes.title: A car outside St. Ann's
scenes.text: Sunday. Mass lets out. Your driver squeezes your arm: a Buick with Pennsylvania plates is idling across from St. Ann's with the engine running, and {second.call}'s car is parked behind it. {lead.call} is nowhere, which is how you know.

choices.label: Back inside. Out through the rectory, and hit back tonight

plus.why: you always know two ways out

whack.why: Shot in his car on Rio Grande Avenue the same night.

crew.why: They came for the boss at church and walked away

choices.result: The priest let you out the rectory door. By midnight {second.first} was dead and {lead.first} was running.
choices.failText: You got out the side door and lived. They got away clean, both of them, and took half the Pacific Avenue book with them.

choices.label: Walk straight at the Buick
choices.hint: Let them see you aren't afraid. They might lose their nerve.

plus.why: his men won't shoot at a man walking at them

crew.why: The boss walked straight at them

choices.result: The Buick pulled away from the curb before you got to it. Everybody on the church steps saw.
choices.failText: They fired and missed. Your driver took one in the shoulder. The police came, and so did the Daily Tide.
